requirements.requirement: Serve working HTTPS on node1 port 8443.
requirements.summary: nginx listened on IPv4 and IPv6 port 8443, returned the expected HTTPS response, presented the configured certificate, and recovered after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Automatically renew the certificate before expiration.
requirements.summary: A certificate expiring within the configured seven-day renewal window was staged, the scheduled daily hook renewed it to a 30-day certificate without a force option, and crond plus the daily schedule persisted across reboot.

requirements.requirement: Load each renewed certificate while continuing to answer HTTPS requests.
requirements.summary: Both forced and expiry-triggered rotations changed the certificate serial served by nginx. Each bounded rotation test completed 100 of 100 HTTPS requests successfully, followed by direct confirmation that nginx served the new certificate.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Alpine 3.23.3 and kernel 6.18.7-0-lts were unchanged before and after implementation and reboot. The installed Alpine nginx/OpenSSL packages and OpenRC integration operated successfully on that platform.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. Certificate renewal and graceful pickup were tested under continuous requests, the platform was retained, and the mandatory node-restart protocol showed a different boot identity followed by recovered services, certificate, configuration, listener, and HTTPS behavior.
limitations: The scheduler was verified through its crontab, running crond service, and direct execution of the exact daily hook; evidence did not wait for the real 02:00 scheduled invocation.
The fixed lifecycle collector does not support Alpine/OpenRC failed-service enumeration, although direct nginx and crond status checks succeeded.
The restart protocol is strong and agrees with fixed boot observations, but this single-node service has no separate cluster state to assess.

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive mutations had a clear task, evidence-collection, corrective, or mandatory-restart role; no causally unrelated mutation was identified. The partially failed setup command created TLS directories and node-ip state that the successful implementation immediately reused. Hygiene is reduced slightly because three executor-created evidence artifacts remained in /tmp: https-rotation-results, https-auto-renew-results, and antrieb-reboot.log. They were useful when created but were not cleaned afterward.
